sourceDesc.p: Public events falling within the span of Cavriana's correspondence, recorded so that the letters can be read against what was happening when they were written.

p.bibl: Wikidata (https://www.wikidata.org). Every identifier here was checked against the item's own label and date before use.

Dates are given in the Julian reckoning the letters themselves use, so that an event and the letters around it can be compared directly. Wikidata states these dates in the proleptic Gregorian calendar, ten days later; the massacre of Saint Bartholomew is 24 August 1572 here and 3 September 1572 there. Each event records the Gregorian form as well, so neither reckoning is lost.

calendar.p: The Julian calendar, in which Cavriana and his correspondents dated their letters. Every date in this file is given in this reckoning.
The Gregorian calendar, ten days ahead of the Julian in this period, and the reckoning Wikidata uses for the same events.

event.label: Peace of Saint-Germain-en-Laye
Paix de Saint-Germain-en-Laye
event.desc: The edict ending the third war of religion, granting the Huguenots four places of safety. Gregorian 18 August 1570. Its slow and contested execution is the subject of most of Cavriana's reporting through the autumn of 1570.

event.label: Marriage of Charles IX and Elisabeth of Austria
event.desc: Celebrated at Mézières. Gregorian 6 December 1570. Cavriana reports the wedding preparations through November and the new queen's reception at court in January.

event.label: Battle of Lepanto
Battaglia di Lepanto
event.desc: The Holy League's naval victory over the Ottoman fleet. Gregorian 17 October 1571.

event.label: Election of Gregory XIII
event.desc: The conclave following the death of Pius V, which elected Ugo Boncompagni. Gregorian 22–23 May 1572.

event.label: Marriage of Henri de Navarre and Marguerite de Valois
event.desc: The match Cavriana had been reporting since 1570, celebrated in Paris six days before the massacre. Gregorian 28 August 1572.

event.label: Massacre of Saint Bartholomew's Day
Massacre de la Saint-Barthélemy
event.desc: The killing of Coligny and the Huguenot leadership in Paris, and afterwards in the provinces. Gregorian 3 September 1572.

event.label: Siege of La Rochelle
event.desc: The royal army's assault on the Huguenot stronghold, lifted when Henri d'Anjou left to take the Polish crown. Gregorian 16 November 1572 to 16 July 1573.

event.label: Siege of Sancerre
event.desc: The eight-month siege of the hilltop town, ended by famine. Gregorian 19 November 1572 to 29 August 1573.

event.label: Election of Henri d'Anjou as King of Poland
event.desc: The first free royal election of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. Gregorian 21 May 1573.

event.label: Conspiracy of Saint-Germain
event.desc: The plot of the Duke of Alençon and the King of Navarre against Charles IX, discovered at Saint-Germain-en-Laye and reported by Cavriana on 6 March 1574. The precise span is uncertain; the dates given bracket the discovery.
